📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games.

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 is everywhere you look. Every news channel is talking about it. Celebrities and musicians are playing GTA 6 or posting about its release. It’s apparently the biggest game ever and has sold nearly 40 million copies already. But if you aren’t a major gamer or not a video game fan at all, you might have questions. I have answers.

Perhaps someone sent you this link because you kept asking them GTA 6 questions. Maybe you did a Google search, made it past the AI results and found this blog explaining what GTA 6 is to people who don’t buy or play games. Whatever the case, welcome. I’m going to walk you through what is almost certainly the biggest video game launch of the decade, why people are going so wild, and what the game actually is and isn’t.

It is an open-world game that mixes together a lot of video game genres, like driving, shooting, and exploration. As with most open-world games, you can run around freely or do story missions. It’s up to the player. You control two characters, Jason and Lucia, who are criminals on the run in fictional versions of Florida and Miami named Leonida and Vice City, respectively.

More or less, yeah. The developer, Rockstar Games, has been working on this game since at least 2015 or so. Turns out creating a photorealistic recreation of a chunk of Florida that players can explore and do whatever they want in takes time!

It has been revealed that no. You can buy it on either PS5 or Xbox for $80. The $100 version comes with a bunch of extra outfits, hairstyles, and other items players can wear or buy in-game using cash they collect from crimes, but it’s definitely not required.

It took me about 90 hours to reach the end of the main story. I’ve since played over 150 hours, and I’m still finding newly introduced stuff, hearing new songs, and seeing new random events. Yeah, it’s significant.

Sources indicate that well, a lot of people have been waiting for 13 years to play GTA 6. The last fresh GTA game, GTA V, was released back in 2013. So anticipation for this game has been building for a long time. And, surprisingly, GTA 6 lived up to the hype.

Sources indicate that there are a few reasons for the glowing critical reception. The game’s narrative is really good, featuring two extremely well-written characters that develop a meaningful relationship over the course of its five chapters. Another significant reason for the high review scores is just how expansive and reactive the world is. Characters in the game will comment on your clothes, respond to your actions, and remember things you did hours and hours ago. It’s also a lot of fun to play, with challenging but rewarding driving, combat, and police encounters. And it looks incredible, with some of the best graphics ever seen in a console game. Some critics are calling it the best game of the year. And many players are calling it one of the best games ever.

GTA: Vice City on the PS2 was much, much smaller and less advanced (though in some ways it was pretty advanced for the time) and was set in the 1980s. While Vice City is a major location in GTA 6, this is an unconnected and different version of the city from that seen in the original 2002 PS2 game.

So many things! Players can steal cars, drive boats, get into fist fights, shoot at the cops, go fishing, play mini-golf, hit the gun range, pet dogs, scuba dive, fly planes, explore the swamps, hunt deer, join in street races, visit the beach, get drunk, buy clothes, play fake video games inside the game, take a shower, eat food, work out, blow up cars, or just chill in a bar. You can also just play through the game’s main story, which is all about Jason and Lucia trying to make some money as criminals to build a life for themselves and their son.

Yes, Jason and Lucia have a child, a fact which was omitted from any pre-release marketing but is revealed in the first 20 minutes of the game. During the events of the game, he is living with his aunt while Lucia and Jason do whatever they can to make a good life for him and get him back.

In a recent development, she is an attractive but disturbing character players meet very early in the game who may or may not be a serial killer or creepy stalker. Despite this, many people online still want to have sex with her. Some players also think Jason should hook up with Mandy and ditch Lucia. These people are wrong.

No. While you can do that stuff, GTA 6 doesn’t force you to be a good boyfriend. You can be a real jerk to Lucia, and she can be a real asshole to Jason. Also, the chores players are talking about only make up a few minutes of the opening hours of GTA 6. The rest of the game has none of that stuff in it.

Industry observers note that like the chores mentioned already, these elements are optional. If you constantly skip working out, your characters will eventually become less ripped and might even develop small bellies and thicker thighs. But you can still play all the missions and shoot cops.

It has been revealed that what? You can totally shoot random people, cops, and more.

Recent findings suggest that that’s not accurate. You can shoot, punch, tackle, burn, run over, drown, choke, and slap women.

Recent findings suggest that uhh, you can steal cars. Some cars, like very fancy cars, have special security measures, so you can’t steal them as easily, but you can walk up to any person driving a car at a stoplight, rip them out and take their ride.

Okay, so, something you need to understand about GTA 6 is that it is at the center of a massive online culture war. Conservative players, grifters, chuds, and other weirdos are currently spreading false information about this game online. There are also plenty of people online posting inflammatory nonsense to get clicks and engagement on sites like Twitter that reward that shit. So if you read something kind of wild about this game, just know it might be false. Check places like Kotaku or other major gaming sites to verify.

Well, actually, Rockstar did remove sex workers you can pay to have sex with from GTA 6. But there are still strippers in the game.

Industry observers note that yes, GTA V has GTA Online, a very popular, successful, and still-ongoing multiplayer game with millions of players. This time around, it seems Rockstar wanted to focus all its resources on getting GTA 6 out the door without also having to finish a major online mode. That said, I find it very hard to believe that GTA 6 won’t get some kind of multiplayer mode in the future.

Never. I mean, officially, Rockstar hasn’t remarked that, but based on how the game looks and how it runs on the Series S, the weakest console it is presently available on, I’m very doubtful a Switch 2 port is coming anytime soon.

Sources indicate that there is a lot of nudity in this game. You can shoot people’s heads off. You can burn them alive. A big part of the game involves robbing stores and selling drugs. I say all that not to suggest your kid or teenager shouldn’t play the game, but just to let you know what’s waiting for them in Vice City. Ultimately, it’s up to you and what you think your kid can handle. Either way, just know they are already totally seeing clips of this game online on places like TikTok.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that according to every Diablo 4 player known to man, I screwed up by skipping its last season.
  • Even though the Season of Hell's Legacy is about to come to an end, Blizzard has delivered good news for me and everyone else who missed it: Most of it will remain in the game permanently.
  • On December 1, when the Season of Tyrael's Gambit begins, all of the unique Prime Evil boss fights will still be available, along with the Diablo world boss, Moophisto, and a handful of Diablo 2-inspired items, including the Hellfire Torch Charm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that according to every Diablo 4 player known to man, I screwed up by skipping its last season. Blizzard shoved just about every iconic Diablo 2 boss and item it could think of into the modern game, and, by all accounts, it was one of the best seasons it ever had.

Even though the Season of Hell's Legacy is about to come to an end, Blizzard has delivered good news for me and everyone else who missed it: Most of it will remain in the game permanently.

On December 1, when the Season of Tyrael's Gambit begins, all of the unique Prime Evil boss fights will still be available, along with the Diablo world boss, Moophisto, and a handful of Diablo 2-inspired items, including the Hellfire Torch Charm. However, the craftable items, like the Enigma chest piece that gives you a free teleport skill, will not carry over.

Even without all the craftable unique items, that's quite a lot of stuff to keep around. Blizzard tends to ditch seasonal additions as soon as a newly introduced season starts, and you usually have to wait a while to see them slipped back into the game in a slightly altered form. The overwhelming excitement around the Diablo 2 content must've convinced Blizzard it was worth putting in the work to keep them around.

Industry observers note that I would've been happy if the portal to Tristram, the rickety old town at the center of Diablo 2, was all that came back. Blizzard pulled off an incredibly faithful remake of it, complete with the old guitar theme and the voice of the blacksmith Griswold. And if you follow the hidden steps to make the Hellfire Torch, you'll be able to visit Uber Tristram, a special version of the town where you can square off against all three of the series' major villains, the Prime Evils, at once.

In a recent development, diablo 4 was always kind of light on hidden quests and bosses, so it's nice to see that Blizzard found a way to bring an notable part of the series back. I'll be curious to see what else comes to the game over the next three years before Diablo 5 arrives. The Amazon class will drop next year, but no expansions are planned to fill the gap. Hopefully Blizzard will take this opportunity to experiment with more things like the Diablo 2 anniversary secrets before it moves onto the sequel.

  • Toby Fox has given eager fans an revision on the development of Deltarune Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 - the Undertale follow-up's final two episodes.
  • According to recent reports, "Chapte 6 is progressing well," he wrote in a new blog post.
  • Sources indicate that while the bones are supposedly all there, Fox explained that he and his team still need to knock out localisation, testing and polishing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toby Fox has given eager fans an revision on the development of Deltarune Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 - the Undertale follow-up's final two episodes.

According to recent reports, "Chapte 6 is progressing well," he wrote in a new blog post. "The game is now a structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end. All the maps, events, and battles exist. (Although there's still one optional event which is dragging out a bit…)".

Sources indicate that while the bones are supposedly all there, Fox explained that he and his team still need to knock out localisation, testing and polishing. "Much of the game looks complete… but, some vital scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing.".

In a recent development, deltarune Chapter 6 was previously described as a slightly shorter episode that should hopefully set up the game's finale quite nicely. Despite being on the smaller side, Fox noted he understandably doesn't want to rush development and "would like it to be as good as possible.".

And since Deltarune's next chapter is almost past the finish line - at least, in some respect - that means certain members of the team have already moved over to Chapter 7.

"Well, we've only just started," Fox continued. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way".

"Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence.".

Deltarune's been on a long journey to get here, but, thankfully, the end is finally in sight. Deltarune debuted as a free download all the way back in 2018, a second chapter then dropped in 2021, the next two launched together four years later, before the arrival of the most recent Chapter 5 this year.

In a recent development, we don't know exactly how long Deltarune's last two chapters might take, but the good news is that it's already been a pretty fantastic game for years. Here's hoping those loose threads don't dangle for much longer.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, much like a huge dust cloud gradually resolving into an army of skull-painted bikers, Paradox's post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld continues to take shape in the course of developer blog posts.
  • Sources indicate that each band has needs, satiation of which makes them feel more motivated and thus, more willing to follow your orders and work for the good of the tribe as a whole.
  • It appears to make for some alarming diversity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, much like a huge dust cloud gradually resolving into an army of skull-painted bikers, Paradox's post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld continues to take shape in the course of developer blog posts. The latest Parablog digs into what I think is one of the game's most interesting aspects – you don't control one single unified civ. Instead, you amass a motley tribe by befriending, conquering, or otherwise assimilating a range of individual wasteland bands.

Sources indicate that each band has needs, satiation of which makes them feel more motivated and thus, more willing to follow your orders and work for the good of the tribe as a whole. Some of the needs are more generic – for example, shelter, nutrition, hydration, medicine, social standing, and security against threats. Others are bespoke, shaped by Custom - another in-game social metric - and by that band's origins.

It appears to make for some alarming diversity. For example, you could have a band that are full vegetarian, and excel at foraging - they won't even eat dried insects, the hippies! You could also have a band of cannibals who have a literal Human Flesh consumption gauge. I see nothing in the latest dev diary to forbid you from assimilating both the cannibals and the vegetarians. Let's, er, not seat them next to each other at the next council meeting, unless we're really running low on finger food.

"All needs can scale by band size, level or other game state elements that make sense," the developers write. "Another thing to keep in mind is that different bands will value different needs depending on who they are or recent events. For example a band that’s experienced extreme hunger will get more motivation from nutrition, while a band on the council will expect to get more standing because of where they are in society, not just because of who they are.

According to recent reports, "When all of these things come together, you are invited to pick which bands are key for your tribe’s goals," the blog continues. "Those bands are the ones you will pay the most attention to motivate. When you look more closely at what those bands actually want you will find narratively and systemically immersive choices to make. At one point a band may care about food because you are facing a famine, but then rumors of some dustland horror beyond the tribe borders scares everyone into caring more about security and downplaying their previous preoccupation with food.".

The most "work-in-progress" part of Afterworld's band motivation system is managing the potential gulf between an individual band's needs and overall tribe policy. You can, for example, put troops in settlements to make bands feel "dominated", which "increases their motivation, bypassing the needs, and allows you to run parts of your tribe with the stick, while others get the carrot.".

In a recent development, the developers are "still iterating on this side of the system, but the intent is for such tactics to [offer] various degrees of sustainability for your tribe, depending on your set up and who your bands are". If you try to coerce a band, you run the risk of them blowing up in rebellion as and when the stick is removed. "This can result in cool moments like you taking down a bigger threatening tribe who’s keeping their lower classes under control through forced medical sedation, but it all comes apart when you find a way to sabotage or raid the source of the sedatives," the blog explains. Seems very fiendish! There are many points of comparison here with other Paradox games, of course. Before writing this piece, I asked Mark for his take on Afterworld based on many hours desecrating the Catholic Church and/or wine trade in Crusader Kings 3. He observed that the game sounds a bit like playing the unlanded leader of some adventurers in CK3. Myself, I wish I could make some precise references to the Europa Universalis series, but our resident expert Brendy (RPS in peace) left many moons ago to found some appalling indepedendent website or other. So I'm going to swing for the fences and say this feels like a continent-scale game of The Sims, except with groups of irradiated and tattooed, neo-Bronze age pillagers instead of smooth-faced burbanites. For the most informed appraisal of all, here's Julian's chat with Paradox about the game's procedural history generation - it writes you a upcoming apocalypse for every playthrough.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the first HBO Lego Harry Potter sets have been revealed, and they're remaking some classic kits... but fans aren't all enthused by the result.

In a recent development, after being teased earlier this year, the initial wave of Lego Harry Potter kits based on HBO's latest series revisits some old haunts; the lineup includes the Gryffindor Common Room, the Hogwarts Express, and Privet Drive. These include new designs and minifigures based on the TV show, but there are obviously similarities to what we've seen before – and that seems to be a sticking point for some. In a Reddit post discussing the sets, the top comment notes that they "they look like bootlegs of the originals lol.".

While there's positive feedback as well (particularly toward Privet Drive's faux-Tudor design), I'm finding just as many negative responses on social media after a quick look through the likes of Instagram. These sets are clearly dividing the community, and I can't imagine it's the reception Lego was hoping for. Here are the kits themselves:.

According to recent reports, the Gryffindor Common Room is a constant throughout the Potter stories, so it makes sense that Lego would remake it here in its newly introduced HBO form. This one is made up of 738 pieces, comes with five minifigures (Harry, Ron, Hermione, Parvati, and Lavender), as well as lots of little details on almost every surface.UK: £79.99 at Lego.

This is probably the most unique of the sets, as the faux-Tudor exterior is quite different from the old movie version. The kit has 545 pieces and four minifigs to go with a brick-built '90s car – Harry, Uncle Vernon, Aunt Petunia, and Dudley. UK: £54.99 at Lego.

What with Harry's first trip to Hogwarts being such a pivotal moment in the story, it makes sense that the Hogwarts Express would feature as a major newly introduced set. This is just the latest in a long line of models recreating this train, and while the engine itself is practically identical, the HBO version of the platform looks like it includes a little cafe waiting area that we've not seen before.UK: £89.99 at Lego.

Recent findings suggest that the final set to be revealed thus far is a BrickHeadz kit, recreating characters in a larger scale. This one has Harry, Malfoy, and Hagrid presumably while they're wandering the Forbidden Forest in detention. It's made up of 380 pieces.UK: £22.99 at Lego.

What Happened To Harrison Ford’s Deckard After Blade Runner 2049? I Asked 2099’s EP For Her Take

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that blade Runner 2049, in my humble opinion, is a science-fiction masterpiece. The Denis Villeneuve-directed sequel not only expertly builds upon Ridley Scott’s 1982 film, but it also adds to the mythology in interesting ways. Additionally, the film includes a stellar performance from Harrison Ford, who reprises his role as Rick Deckard. In the near decade since the film’s release, I’ve been wondering about Deckard’s ultimate fate. So, when CinemaBlend spoke to the creator of Blade Runner 2099, I asked for her take.

Deckard serves as more of a supporting character in Villeneuve’s heavily praised film, which reveals the former Blade Runner to be in hiding in the ruins of Las Vegas 30 years after the events of the OG film. Found by Replicant Runner K (Ryan Gosling), Deckard is eventually revealed to have fathered a child with his late replicant partner, Rachel. That child is eventually revealed to be replicant-memory-maker Dr. Ana Stelline (Carla Juri), with whom Deckard reunites at the end of the film, thanks to K.

Since walking out of the theater after seeing the film for the first time in 2017, I’ve wondered about Deckard and Ana’s fates, especially with the looming war between humans and Replicants. Blade Runner 2099 creator/showrunner Silka Luisa is also a major fan of the franchise and, when she was asked for her take on what happened to Ana and Deckard, she shared some surprising comments with CB:.

I never asked Michael Green, because I'm sure — he was the screenwriter for 2049, and there's just no world [where] he didn't know what happens. But I almost didn't want to know. What I love about Blade Runner is that so much of it can exist in your own mind, and the world feels so rich that it inspires you to create your own stories within it. And something about that period not being totally defined is exciting, because we can all suggest different things. Yeah, so I don't have a definitive answer.

Considering how massive a Blade Runner fan Luisa is, I’m honestly shocked over her not asking Michael Green (who shares 2049 writing credits with Hampton Fancher) for a definitive answer on Deckard and Ana. I can, however, also see Luisa’s point, though, as this franchise does leave certain plot threads open-ended, leading to fan speculation. This answer also tracks with the EP’s approach to 2099, which is a standalone piece that doesn’t have direct references to its big-screen predecessors.

While Blade Runner’s ending remains controversial in some circles, the discussions surrounding 2049’s conclusion arguably aren’t as tense. Villeneuve’s film went through different alterations during development, and even the ending changed. Fancher previously disclosed that the original initiative was for Deckard to die. While that could’ve been powerful (if crafted effectively), I’m fine with Deckard not biting the substantial one, considering it leaves the door open for a direct sequel. And Silka Luisa is down for that as well:.

Industry observers note that I really hope they make another. I really hope they make a sequel, just as a fan, to be honest.

For right now, though, fans can return to this dark, futuristic universe by way of 2099. The limited series centers on dying Replicant Blade Runner Olwen (played by Michelle Yeoh) and Cora (Hunter Schafer), a human posing as a Replicant. While fans won’t be getting answers on Deckard, the show covers plenty of ground in other respects. And, who knows, maybe we’ll actually get that 2049 sequel one day.

All episodes of Blade Runner 2099 will begin streaming for Prime Video subscription holders on November 25 amid the 2026 TV schedule. Blade Runner 2049 can also at the moment be streamed on Prime, and it’s available to watch for free on Tubi.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that after waiting three years for Relic to expand Firm of Heroes 3's singleplayer, watching DLC after DLC focused on expanding the roster of units available in multiplayer matches, Operation Torch looks like a welcome addition.
  • Recent findings suggest that having played through the whole thing, I really want to say it's been worth the wait.
  • Recent findings suggest that about halfway through the campaign, I'm put in charge of managing a retreat under a German advance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that after waiting three years for Relic to expand Firm of Heroes 3's singleplayer, watching DLC after DLC focused on expanding the roster of units available in multiplayer matches, Operation Torch looks like a welcome addition. It's a upcoming 15-mission campaign set in North Africa. following two US officers as they try to break the German Afrika Korps' hold on the region.

Recent findings suggest that having played through the whole thing, I really want to say it's been worth the wait. Unfortunately, it's not so straightforward as that.

Recent findings suggest that about halfway through the campaign, I'm put in charge of managing a retreat under a German advance. While I must use my limited forces to hold back enemy troops at the head of the map, I'm also to drive a supply truck to different structures on the map so its crew can evacuate the buildings. It's a fraught start to the mission, forcing me to balance my attentions on the embattled front while also keeping a watchful eye on the vulnerable supply truck. German forces are seeping past the line and it would only take one well-placed anti-tank gun to spell an end to the evacuation.

Industry observers note that the tension that comes in those moments, where I'm hopping about the battlefield barely holding things together, is Tech giant of Heroes at its best. Operation Torch has several moments that reach that height of trying to command chaos, but they're squandered just as promptly as they come.

When the three structures are broken down, I'm ordered to pull back to a hill outside of town. The mission isn't over, though: German officers are sifting through the abandoned buildings, looking for intel that was missed in the evacuation, and I'm to take two squads of snipers into enemy territory to kill them before they find anything. While it sounds exciting on paper, the mechanics of the mission's scripting make the reality underwhelming. My weakened army is sitting on a hill outside of town but no Germans come their way. In town, German units either stand still or travel in small looping patrols. Navigating the camouflaged sniper squads between them is easy work, but slow going. And even when they come out of stealth to shoot the officers and are spotted by a unit of German soldiers, they walk away from the fight and the Germans don't give chase. This may all be because I'm playing on standard difficulty, but the AI is oddly passive throughout Operation Torch.

Sources indicate that across multiple missions, I repeatedly used the same cheesing tactic. I would send a unit with the stealth passive to hide invisibly behind cover near the enemy, with strict orders not to open fire. With my infiltrator acting as a forward spotter, I'd then pummel the enemy with mortars from a safe distance. This tactic worked again and again. I knew, really, that it was no fun to do – turning every battle into a slow grinding down of the enemy – but it was also too effective to ignore when the enemy would never fight back.

Industry observers note that it's a shame so many of Operation Torch's missions hit a bum, overly-scripted note because I really enjoyed their unfurling narrative. Admittedly, my military history is poor, and all my knowledge of the North Africa campaign is drawn from the bits in SAS Rogue Heroes before they go to Europe, but my general understanding is that it was a campaign that saw rapid advances turn into just-as-quick retreats. This plays into Operation Torch's missions where success often isn't pushing the front forwards, but holding the line while covering routed allied forces, or defending a pass long enough for air support to arrive and cause enough damage to force the Germans to slow down. And, because you're battling backwards and forwards over the same territory, Relic employ one of my favourite RTS tricks: throwing you back into the same map but from a different perspective. In one mission you may be on the assault, prizing free the Afrika Korps' grip on a town street by street, but then a few missions later you find yourself defending the same territory from a retaliatory attack. It's unfortunate that the same push and pull isn't as evident on the battlefield.

Relic are experimenters, often reinventing a game's systems between entries in a series or trying out a fresh mechanic in their expansions. In Operation Torch, the new toy is a choice of unlocks at the end of each mission. After a tank-focused assignment, for instance, you're offered a choice between a passive perk that makes Shermans 25% harder to hit while moving, or another which unlocks a different Sherman variant in your motor pool. Complete the map's optional objective and you also get to choose between a 10% reduction in tank costs and an upgrade that sees all your tanks produced at level 3 veterancy. These perks then apply throughout your campaign. By the final mission, the right side of your screen is a fat stack of passive and active perks. It's a neat idea but, in practice, it didn't seem to make a dramatic difference to how I played. I do like the idea of gradually developing your forces capabilities over a campaign but perhaps the difference needs to be more dramatic. Making your tanks slightly cheaper or harder to hit doesn't make that much of a tangible difference when you're right in there amidst the tracks and trenches.

Thus, it really does fall back to the strength of Operation Torch's missions, which are sometimes great but too often a case of rolling over the enemy very, very slowly. Perhaps this is a game best played with the difficulty whacked up high.

According to recent reports, while I was hoping for more from Operation Torch, mind, I do hope it's not the last time we see Relic flesh out Tech giant of Heroes 3's singleplayer. There's still plenty of scope there, and plenty of room for further experiments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 - one from unofficial sources, at least - may be closer than we thought.
  • Sources indicate that "The exe is out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 - one from unofficial sources, at least - may be closer than we thought. After suddenly returning last week with a near-full build of the Xbox version, notorious leaker CyberLeek has now posted the missing piece they intentionally held back: the game's executable (.exe) file.

Sources indicate that "The exe is out. Always free. An early Christmas gift from CL," CyberLeek reportedly wrote, as relayed on Reddit. "The torch passes to the open source re-comp and emulation projects.".

Hours later, the recompilation modders and hackers part of the Project Leonida Discord server - the current hub for all GTA 6 recompilation efforts - posted footage of the game booting up on PC.

In just a matter of hours, modders - with the help of Claude AI - managed to turn the leaked Xbox build into a PC port, of sorts. In this Reddit video, you can see the game boot up to the initial setup before hitting a black screen. The build is clearly not yet playable, though Eurogamer has not directly verified those claims.

Shayder, one of the lead developers on Project Leonida, said in a since-deleted post on X that we should "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon." On the project's Discord server, they later clarified that it could take about a week for the build to reach a playable state on PC.

As for CyberLeek, the leaker is still soliciting donations for a secret project "for the gamers", adding in the build's readme file, "Nobody has to give anything, and every release stays free either way. But every donation is a vote for more of this, and so is every trade of the token.".

It has been revealed that rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA 6, but the firm has historically released its games on PC several months after their console debut. In October, a report noted GTA 6's PC version would arrive in the first quarter of 2027, an unusually short gap between the console and PC releases.

It has been revealed that these latest recompilation efforts, however, may force Rockstar to speed up development of the PC version. Though the recompiled build may never reach the level of quality or stability of an official port, many of those eager to play the game on PC likely wouldn't care.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Enhancement 11/25/26 03:11 PM: One project fork, AvatarManz, now claims to run early portions of GTA 6 at 16 fps average. We've updated the "top five" projects according to Portwatch VI.

Things are moving fast. Now that an illicit Xbox build of GTA 6 is out in the wild, anonymous modders are racing to port it to PC, and the work is progressing faster than many expected. At this rate, it's possible that a static recompilation of GTA 6 will run on a PC in a matter of days. It's also possible it will take much longer to produce a playable build that's actually on par with the console versions.

What we do know for sure is that Rockstar is taking notice and has already begun cracking down on the highest-profile projects. As always, downloading pirated software is illegal and can infect your PC with malware, and that last bit is doubly true in the dubious AI era we now live in.

For now, the only thing to do is observe and report. Here's where things stand with GTA 6 PC ports.

Several projects have made it as rendering and playing early portions of the game at low framerates (10-16 fps average), but it's hard to verify clips making the rounds when so many are obvious fakes.

Recent findings suggest that dozens of groups of anonymous modders and vibecoders. So many, in fact, that several websites dedicated to tracking the progress of GTA 6 recomp efforts have also appeared. One of the tracker sites, Portwatch VI, has a list of projects ranked by their "playable" completion percentage—best not to take those made up figures as an accurate estimate of when a port will be complete. The top five are:.

Until very recently, the Leonida project was among those making impressive progress, but the group's creator (a 15-year-old) quit the project after Rockstar got its Discord server taken down.

Keep up to date with the most key stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Every GTA 6 recomp project is based on the same thing: An illicit Xbox build of GTA 6 released online by Cyberleek, the notorious leaker who previously shared video of a GTA 6 development build months before its release.

With GTA 6 being the biggest game in the world at the moment and not available on PC, there is an outsized motivation to get it running.

A recomp refers to static recompilation, which is the result of reverse-engineering a game's code to make it run on other hardware (usually a PC). If you want to read further on how that's achieved, PCG alum Wes Fenlon's excellent Read Only Memo newsletter has what you're looking for.

As for how GTA 6 ports (and ports for other fresh games) are coming together so rapidly, the answer is AI. The advent of AI coding tools like Claude have greatly expedited the work required to create a static recompilation of games on another platform. What used to take months to years now takes hours to days. Recomps that heavily use AI are often buggier, messier, and have fewer features than human-made fan projects, but they are fast and functional.

It's way too early to speak in absolutes, but I'm comfortable assuming that the first "playable" recomps will require an exceptionally powerful PC.

That guess is based on GTA 6 being an obviously demanding game and also some recent precedent: The earliest Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake recomps that've appeared online have high system requirements to perform as well as it does natively on Switch 2—and, well, GTA 6 has a lot more happening under the hood than a 28-year-old Zelda game.

That's the big question. My money is on no, it won't. To switch up plans on a dime would assume that Rockstar is sitting on a polished PC version that it could put out any day, and I'm not convinced that's the case. The current rumor, preceding all of this leak business, is that the PC version of GTA 6 is planned for Q1 2027 (so anytime before April).

That's not to say Rockstar couldn't expedite the process if it wanted to—they certainly have the resources to achieve the unlikely.

Latest Update: Microsoft reportedly looked into killing paid multiplayer for next-gen Xbox Helix consoles

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (443 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A upcoming report from Windows Central details how Xbox was reportedly looking into removing the paywall that prevents players without Xbox Live from playing online games, only to potentially renege on its decision sometime during production of the next-gen device.
  • It has been revealed that "Sources close to Microsoft's plans tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer," says the Windows Central report.
  • It has been revealed that the revised plan has reportedly been altered thanks to a myriad of factors affecting the Xbox business: newly introduced management, rising component costs, and a shifting hardware strategy, are all outlined specifically in the report.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A upcoming report from Windows Central details how Xbox was reportedly looking into removing the paywall that prevents players without Xbox Live from playing online games, only to potentially renege on its decision sometime during production of the next-gen device.

It has been revealed that "Sources close to Microsoft's plans tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer," says the Windows Central report. It goes on to note that this Xbox Live-free plan was iterated upon under Xbox's previous leadership, but with Asha Sharma's appointment as Xbox head in February, all that apparently changed. I guess she did promise "radically different business models", after all.

It has been revealed that the revised plan has reportedly been altered thanks to a myriad of factors affecting the Xbox business: newly introduced management, rising component costs, and a shifting hardware strategy, are all outlined specifically in the report. We've previously heard that Xbox's next-gen console could cost up to $1,800, with a handheld version coming in 2027 and a full release by holiday 2028 (a Helix console at $1,200 would mean a 50 percent increase on top of Series X's current price, for what it's worth). Sharma has stressed Helix will launch as "a family of devices" that will act as a bridge between PC and Xbox capable of playing games from both platforms.

Sources indicate that if Xbox has, indeed, decided to scrap the idea of free online multiplayer access, it'll be a blow to the idealistic 'PC and Xbox' platform that Microsoft has been touting for the past few years: PC players do not need a subscription in order to access online modes, so - right out the gate - there will be a division between one group of players and the other. Perhaps this is why we've heard a little change in the tone of how Sharma and other Xbox bosses are talking about Helix more recently - these hints that the console will be a true PC-and-console hybrid have died down, and been replaced by insinuations that we'll see more of a traditional console with the "ability to play your PC games.".

Xbox has been running Xbox Live as a service since 2002, when it launched on the original Xbox console. By 2005, it was split into gold and silver tiers to distinguish free players from those that paid. In 2023, the service was fully renamed Xbox Game Pass Core, looping in access to the base roster of Game Pass games with online play.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that nvidia may have finally released a proper cure for their last graphics driver, 621.24, reportedly writing unneccesarily vast amounts of data to some consumers' SSDs. A hotfix late last week seemed to have made things better, but not fixed everything. Here's hoping driver 621.40 has managed to totally rectify things.

Alongside delivering enhancements specifically aimed at Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4, Where Winds Meet, and Assetto Corsa Rally, 621.40 lists dealing with the fact "excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background" as one of its key aims.

Recent findings suggest that as to whether or not it's achieved that, some folks on Reddit and the Nvidia forum look to be making yes-shaped noises, but I'd not quite classify what I've seen so far as 100% proof. If you've reverted to the last driver which looked issue free, 621.01, waiting a few more days and seeing if a more definitive consensus emerges might be the best option.

After all, the hotfix which preceded 621.40 also declared war against those excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg, and it ended up stopping the excessive writing from starting right after you boot up and reducing the amount that's written, but not totally getting rid of the problem if an affected PC was left running for extended periods. At the very least, the fact the attempts at fixing the matter have now made their way into Nvidia's main branch is a key step towards the latest driver to hit the manufacturer's site and app eventually being excessive write-free.

Industry observers note that as we've noted in our previous coverage of the problem, which doesn't seem to be affecting all machines, if you want to check if you're suffering from the excessive writing you'll need to open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do some maths to work out if it's writing little scraps of MB or major bits of GB.

As Inside the NBA’s latest season on ESPN continues, questions continue to swirl around the show in regard to its future. Longtime co-host Ernie Johnson has officially confirmed his plans to leave the show at the end of this season, and colleague Charles Barkley apparently plans to do the same. There’s been a lot of discussion regarding who might replace the beloved sports commentators, and Barkley recently pitched his successor. While it’s a solid pick, I’d admittedly prefer to see another seasoned pundit take over Barkley’s post.

Barkley – also known as “The Round Mound of Rebound” to some – is definitely someone who loves to speak his mind. So it doesn’t surprise me at all that he’d have thoughts on who might be able to take his place on Inside. The former Phoenix Sun was recently quoted as saying he didn’t believe anyone but fellow ex-player Jalen Rose could replace him at the desk. That comment was brought up to Rose when he was interviewed by Front Office Sports (as seen on YouTube) and, when asked about the job, he said this:.

I love Charles and yes, that would be something that I would be interested in. The one thing I learned about this business is everything isn't transactional. If Charles Barkley is going to say into a microphone that you're the person that he feels like should replace him, you can't write a check for that. Even if it never happens. And so, for him to say that, it's priceless. I'm so very gracious.

The notion of Rose taking over for Barkley is actually quite reasonable, considering his resume as a broadcaster. He’s not only served as a fill-in analyst for Inside the NBA for years now, but he’s also taken on hosting duties for ABC/ESPN over the years. I personally enjoy seeing Rose when he appears on Inside, and his relaxed demeanor usually serves as a firm counterbalance to others on the dais like the vivacious Barkley or Shaquille O’Neal. With that said, there’s another recurring analyst I’d love to see join the show instead.

Inside has welcomed plenty of insightful and entertaining guest hosts over the years, from the cool Vince Carter to the wise-cracking Draymond Green (who has a rivalry with Charles Barkley). Someone who, for me, has always been a welcome presence on the show is Chris Webber, who’s been appearing on the show for years. He obviously has plenty of broadcasting experience, and he’s a wealth of knowledge when it comes to basketball. I’d say the show would be lucky to have him full-time.

It has been revealed that again, though, this isn’t to say that Jalen Rose wouldn’t be able to do the job effectively. There may actually be a reality in which both players end up on the show full time by next season. However, that’s assuming ESPN is looking to bring on two former players and not get another non-ex-player analyst to specifically fill the void that’ll be left by Johnson.

In a recent development, to be honest, it may also behoove me not to get too ahead of myself right now, as the season is still young. Also, while Charles Barkley’s retirement claim is seeming more likely, he hasn’t said much more about it in the wake of Ernie Johnson’s announcement. We’ll just have to wait and see what happens and how the producers choose to proceed should Barkley leave the fold along with Johnson.

Latest Update: GTA 6 rewards empathy because being a "demigod stomping through the world" is only fun for so long

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (820 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 is the first game in the series to make me feel bad, like really bad, for yeeting innocent cyclists into the Gulf of Leonida with the velocity of a pickup truck at 120 miles per hour.
  • Rockstar intentionally designed GTA 6 with a built-in criminal profile system that discourages what in-game warnings describe as "psycho" behavior, which is also a permanent label you can acquire if you act like I do consistently without save-scumming.
  • "I think as the resolution goes up, it sort of asks different new questions," indicates Nelson.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is the first game in the series to make me feel bad, like really bad, for yeeting innocent cyclists into the Gulf of Leonida with the velocity of a pickup truck at 120 miles per hour. It doesn't stop me from doing it, but every time I find myself covering my mouth with my hand in horror and loading up a previous save, preserving the innocence of a Jason or Lucia without the human-shaped blood splatter on their truck hood. Empathy is another word for the feeling I have toward Leonidans, and it's very much by design.

Rockstar intentionally designed GTA 6 with a built-in criminal profile system that discourages what in-game warnings describe as "psycho" behavior, which is also a permanent label you can acquire if you act like I do consistently without save-scumming. This evolution from Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system is a first for the GTA series and a minor point of contention amid unanimous praise for the game, but Rockstar co-founder Rob Nelson tells Eurogamer that it's simply more fun to play the game as if the NPCs whizzing around the world are actual people. It certainly helps that they look pretty darn close to real humans this time around.

"I think as the resolution goes up, it sort of asks different new questions," indicates Nelson. "As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics. So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun ... It's fun for some people like myself to just sort of role-play in the world, and be in the world, and restraint becomes something you hadn't thought about.".

Industry observers note that empathy is a bit of a contradiction to the old GTA fantasy of rampaging indiscriminately through a city helpless to your whimsy, but Nelson is right that there's so much more depth to GTA 6 that makes that sort of stuff feel one-dimensional by comparison. Even compared to GTA 5, I find myself exponentially more immersed cruising around Leonidas, and a lot of that comes down to how lifelike its inhabitants are.

Sources indicate that "If you think about the NPCs, even back to [GTA] 5, you would draw a weapon - first of all, they didn't react if you drew an invisible shotgun out of nowhere, or a rocket launcher," Nelson says. "They don't react unless you aim it, and then they flee in terror, and you're just sort of this demigod stomping through the world, you know? And that's fun, but for how long?".

In a recent development, if the answer to that question for you is, 'endlessly', you can still choose that life in GTA 6, but you'll eventually reach an irreversible stage in your criminal profile that will permanently alter the way NPCs react and interact with you. "You choose. You're trying to jack somebody off a motorcycle, and they pull a gun on you, and you have to blow their head off and it's like, 'You shouldn't have made me do that!'" Nelson says.

According to recent reports, "And so then it has more meaning, and it's more funny in a way when it's a little bit more pointed. And you can still go on those rampages and basically smash your Criminal Profile until it breaks and then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically says 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'".

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

In a recent development, it's a testament to GTA 6's strong writing that I care far too much about Jason and Lucia's relationship to let either of them reach that point in the game's honor system. I'll probably never resist the urge to hijack a nice car in a GTA game, but in this latest iteration, I'll pretty much always load up an old save afterward and role-play as a petty criminal at worst.

For those of you out there in love with Grand Theft Auto 6's soundtrack, you'll be happy to know that Rockstar Games have revealed an additional 23 tracks as part of the game's deluxe edition album.

These tracks, available via streaming services, include songs from artists like HEALTH, Denzel Curry, Playboi Carti, and more. You can find the full track list on the official Rockstar Games music website.

Some of these artists played a significant role in the game. Justice, for example, helped compose the game's original soundtrack and several of their tracks appear throughout the game. There are others, too.

Industry observers note that both Sexyy Red and Denzel Curry voice characters in the game's later chapters. Others like Kodack Black and Freddie Gibbs also show up, too - that's not to mention the huge number of musicians who make an appearance in the game's many radio stations. If you listen through those, you'll hear the voices of Keith Richards, Lana Del Ray, The Alchemist and others.

Sources indicate that musical talent also played an additional role in creating the TV advertisements and demonstrates you can watch in the game. Zack Fox is one example, as is Weird Al Yankovic. Both wrote parts of the game's enticing and absurd substantial screen entertainment - which makes sense given the pair's shared comedy background.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sony's revealed staggering statistics relating to the popularity of Grand Theft Auto on PlayStation 5, not least that more than 39 million unique people have played the game there.
  • Unsurprisingly, with such massive numbers, GTA 6 is a record-breaker on PlayStation.
  • Industry observers note that in addition, PlayStation also saw "the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day" since the console's launch, outside of end-of-year holidays, suggesting that Rockstar's latest game, more than any other PS5 game released so far, has driven hardware sales.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sony's revealed staggering statistics relating to the popularity of Grand Theft Auto on PlayStation 5, not least that more than 39 million unique people have played the game there. That's more than the official GTA 6 day-one sales tally of 32.5m copies across all platforms.

Unsurprisingly, with such massive numbers, GTA 6 is a record-breaker on PlayStation. According to the PlayStation Blog, the game has recorded the highest number of concurrent players on PlayStation ever, surpassing any previous record across all kinds of game - multiplayer, free-to-play and single-player.

Industry observers note that in addition, PlayStation also saw "the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day" since the console's launch, outside of end-of-year holidays, suggesting that Rockstar's latest game, more than any other PS5 game released so far, has driven hardware sales. GTA 6 is apparently the first game played on 70 percent of newly introduced PS5 consoles.

The average GTA 6 playtime, per person, is a considerable 17.4 hours, the blog says, and the total number of hours spent playing the game is 683 million - a number so high I can't contextualise it.

It has been revealed that microsoft hasn't declared equivalent data for Xbox but I assume the game is a record-breaker there, too, given that it broke pre-order Xbox Store records in the same way GTA 6 did on PlayStation. However, GTA 6 is estimated to have sold far more copies on PlayStation - as many as 75 percent of its total sales, according to Alinea Analytics analyst Rhys Elliott.

According to recent reports, elliott estimated that GTA 6 amassed a colossal 44.9m sales by the end of its opening weekend, and that 33.7m of those were on PlayStation 5 (which still doesn't reach the '39 million unique players' stat Sony has just trotted out) and 11.2m were on Xbox. That amount of sales would earn Rockstar something like $4bn in revenue.

According to recent reports, the arrival of GTA 6 has, then, been seismic. The game has wowed critics and dominated conversation not only in the games industry but also across entertainment news and mainstream news. Meanwhile, however, we await the verdict in the Rockstar Games employment tribunal in Scotland, relating to the sudden firing of 34 employees a year ago. Was Rockstar union-busting, as alleged? It'll be a historic ruling if deemed so.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that nvidia's latest GeForce Game Ready driver, version 621.40, is out now. "This new Game Ready Driver provides the best gaming experience for Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4, and Assetto Corsa Rally," the notes say, "and the addition of DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering to Where Winds Meet.".

It has been revealed that which is kind of burying the lead. This patch is really a hotfix for a hotfix, an update that finally addresses the bug with previous driver packages that had them pointlessly rewriting a log file over and over, promptly adding up to tens of GB every hour and potentially damaging SSDs nobody can afford to replace any more.

Sources indicate that over the weekend Nvidia released a hotfix that supposedly caught the bug, only for users to discover it merely delayed its onset. Rather than setting in immediately after a reboot, it would wait until your PC had been on for a while before shitting the bed. If you're one of the people who leaves your computer running overnight then I hope you stayed on version 621.01, the last safe driver package before the current one.

According to recent reports, forum users have been testing out version 621.40 and it seems to have not only stopped the Nvidia container service from freaking out and rewriting its log, but also caught a bug with custom cursors that would make them turn gray. Which is nice.

I'm tempted to play it safe and stay on my old driver anyway, though I'll revision for Dawn of War 4, which comes out on December 3. People with the Commander Edition can jump in early on November 30, and readers in the US and UK can enter our competition to win a Steam code for the Commander Edition right now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I'm not sure I would've ever expected William Shatner to be mentioned in the same breath as Grand Theft Auto VI, but that's what's been happening as of late. A viral clip recently showed Shatner besmirching the recently released game, and it generated a bit of backlash. Now, Shatner is speaking out about the brouhaha. Frankly, I'm surprised the 95-year-old actor even knew what it was, and based on his latest comments, I'm still unsure whether he does.

It has been revealed that as Star Trek fans may be well aware, Shatner is relatively unafraid to offer an opinion on subjects he's not completely familiar with. He's landed in hot water before offering up tons of commentary on Trek, despite never watching the shows, and now, a clip of him talking about the game on Piers Morgan Uncensored is making waves. The host prompted Shatner for his opinion on Grand Theft Auto VI, and he noted the following:.

No! I think it's the dumbest thing I've ever heard! Why don't you read a good book?

It has been revealed that as one might expect, some people took offense to Shatner and other commentators' words on the program. This is, after all, a game that has made more than Taylor Swift's Eras tour in under a week. Comments on the clip popped up on X, and they were critical of all involved:.

The comments called out various claims, mainly the assertion that Grand Theft Auto VI is simply a "pimp simulator." Of course, it was previously declared that the game would not allow prostitution, which was featured in previous releases.

According to recent reports, william Shatner seemed to catch wind of the negative comments and was quick to respond on his personal X account. He wanted to say that his comments were not meant to be inflammatory to the game or gamers, but rather to the four panelists that he had to sit and watch before doing his own segment:.

Last week there were a bucketful of nasty replies on this video clip where most of the angry “children” took the quote as a general statement but didn’t bother to see what I was referring to as ridiculous. Prior to my segment, there was a segment on GTA. Look at these 4 that got airtime 👇🏻! 🙄 Unfortunately, they probably don’t know how to read, especially the guy in 🕶️. That’s who they got to represent gamers. That’s what the comment was about. I had to suffer watching them it was ridiculous! 😤😑.

It has been revealed that I'm hoping Shatner isn't stressed about this, because I know I'm not personally concerned about what opinion he holds on Grand Theft Auto VI. In fact, I would expect most people north of 90 years old would not be too interested in video games and would sooner read a book.

Industry observers note that what I am interested in, however, are William Shatner's thoughts on past co-stars and what he has to say about space and life in general. Fortunately, he's often doing that as well as making frequent trips around the world to talk to anyone who will listen about his past feuds and time in Hollywood.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Grand Theft Auto VI is available to purchase right now, and William Shatner is frequently on the web offering up his opinion. I'm honestly still tickled that this whole situation even happened, and I love it when two pieces of pop culture I love intersect in an unexpected way.

One especially impressive element of Grand Theft Auto 6 is how many of its little mechanics interact with each other. As you can see below, if you bring a vehicle with a winch to a cash machine, you can actually pull it off the wall and drag it away from the scene of the crime.

Why rob a bank in GTA 6 when you can just take the whole ATM💸 How to do it❓- Hook the ATM up to a vehicle with a winch- Drag it through the streets until the cash cases fall out- Shoot them open and get out fast, the cops come rapidly!(via u/MelloYello917) pic.twitter.com/5eXbULJWP3.

As you progress through Grand Theft Auto 6, the game actually introduces you to both styles of heists. Without spoiling exactly how this happens, you're told how to go about taking on such criminal ventures, and you can continue to do so throughout the game at your pleasure. Still, even after you've been tutorialised, pulling off one of these heists is no joke, and can easily turn chaotic.

This GTA 6 robbery sequence was CRAZY, I couldn't even think straight . pic.twitter.com/l65xSFRoSr.

Here's a little tip for those of you looking to pull off a heist yourself. You're told that safety deposit boxes can be rifled through for additional loot. However, when you actually make your way into a vault, these will be closed without much sign on which you can access. If you use the focus mode (by pushing in both L3 and R3), it will highlight boxes which you can shoot open. This, of course, may garner unwanted attention, so whether or not you think it's worth doing is part of the risk/reward dilemma you'll have to reckon with. As is the case with so much stuff in GTA 6 including, but not limited to, car-jacking.

If you're looking to get your life of crime properly underway, you can read our GTA 6 robberies page for a breakdown on how it works. Alternatively, for a wider view of the game, our GTA 6 walkthrough is the way to go.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The premature death of BioWare is made even sadder by the fact that many of its best games were never remastered or remade for modern hardware, and now they probably never will be. Compare that to an RPG studio like Bethesda, which is notorious for endlessly remastering, re-releasing, and porting The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim, and it's easy to see why BioWare diehards feel like they were dealt a bad hand by the studio's parent organization, EA.

Not to rub salt into the wound, but former Dragon Age lead Mark Darrah, a BioWare veteran who worked at the studio for more than two decades, Dragon Age: Origins could've easily been remastered and probably would've sold pretty well if it weren't for EA's reluctance to remake or remaster anything.

It has been revealed that talking to Pembridge TV (timestamp), Darrah says a big reason EA doesn't typically modernize its older games is because a big portion of its IP catalog is annual sports games like EA Sports FC and NHL. "What are you gonna take NHL 2005 and do a 20th anniversary remaster? What? You have an NHL. NHL never went away. Madden never went away. Football Club never went away," Darrah says.

That doesn't explain why series like Mass Effect and Dragon Age didn't get more remasters (on that, Darrah simply states "they don't get it"), but Darrah says the opportunity was there even if Skyrim levels of ports wouldn't work.

"Honestly, yeah, I don't know that anyone other than Bethesda could get away with porting Skyrim to every single platform and selling a million copies every single time they do that," he says, adding, "But yes! We could have remastered Origins probably twice and sold a couple million copies each time.".

Former Dragon Age lead indicates EA mismanagement killed BioWare by forcing it into terrible choices: "They made us do something".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar Games is seemingly interested in expanding Red Dead Redemption beyond video games, after years of Hollywood knocking on its doors.
  • In a recent development, the information comes from a new report in The Ankler, citing agents in the know.
  • Rockstar, however, is not interested in turning Grand Theft Auto into a movie or TV show, per the same report.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games is seemingly interested in expanding Red Dead Redemption beyond video games, after years of Hollywood knocking on its doors. According to a fresh report, the tech giant is looking for someone to pick up the movie and TV rights for its open-world Westerner series.

In a recent development, the information comes from a new report in The Ankler, citing agents in the know. According to the report, Rockstar wanted something in the range of $100m (£76m) as a minimum for the license to its Red Dead Redemption series of games. As the report pointed out, Amazon paid $250m (£191m) in 2017 for Lord of the Rings' TV show rights alone.

Rockstar, however, is not interested in turning Grand Theft Auto into a movie or TV show, per the same report. It's not clear why the manufacturer is willing to entertain the idea for one franchise and not the other, but the vastly larger popularity of GTA (compared to RDR, at least) could explain why.

It's worth noting that streamers like Netflix and Amazon have been on something of a hot streak recently with the success of demonstrates based on popular video games, such as Fallout. HBO managed to turn The Last of Us into a prestige series that can attract both fans of the game and casual TV viewers.

According to recent reports, indeed, many more video game-based highlights are in the works, like Amazon's Tomb Raider series, its God of War adaptation, as well as FX's Far Cry anthology show. Even Call of Duty, a massive - though nowhere near as massive as GTA - franchise, is getting a live-action movie in 2028.

But none of those are as profitable or culturally-dominnant as Grand Theft Auto. GTA 6 just released, and immediately beat analyst expectations. The game made $3.79bn (£2.90bn) in revenue on day one off the back of 32.5m copies sold, making it the biggest launch of any entertainment product in history, so it's understandable why Rockstar is not too eager to turn it into a movie or TV show.

As reported by ABC 7, parade officials won’t make a decision until early Thursday morning, before the start of the parade. One option is to fly balloons much lower to the ground. Another option being floated by officials is to start the parade earlier than 8:30 am to hopefully avoid the worst of the incoming storm.

“You may remember, there was some lightning and storms coming through on July 4th. It’s been that kind of year. The fireworks were moved up a little bit. That is one option. If the weather is coming in a little later, can we start things a little earlier?” mentioned Farrell.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • CD Projekt made its Q3 2026 financial report today, and there's not a whole lot to see: The Witcher 3 remaster was a big hit, work on Cyberpunk 2 and The Witcher 4 is ticking along, and everyone really liked Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2.
  • Perhaps understandably, a number of questions in the subsequent investors call put the focus on Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • "Obviously, this is a call about us, not about Rockstar, but I do understand the connection here," Nowakowski said when asked if The Witcher 4 will represent a technological leap over its predecessor comparable to GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CD Projekt made its Q3 2026 financial report today, and there's not a whole lot to see: The Witcher 3 remaster was a big hit, work on Cyberpunk 2 and The Witcher 4 is ticking along, and everyone really liked Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2.

Perhaps understandably, a number of questions in the subsequent investors call put the focus on Grand Theft Auto 6. While CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski didn't go too deep on the topic, he did say that the upcoming Witcher 4 will be comparable to GTA 6 in at least one way.

"Obviously, this is a call about us, not about Rockstar, but I do understand the connection here," Nowakowski said when asked if The Witcher 4 will represent a technological leap over its predecessor comparable to GTA 6. "Having said that, of course, I'm not going to make a deep dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course, we did look at the game. We did see the differences.

"Do we believe there's going to be a comparable leap between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4? I think so, yes. I mean, it's been 11 years. We are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game. So yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4.".

Recent findings suggest that well, sure. As Nowakowski stated, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt was released 11 years ago, and it'll be two more years before The Witcher 4 comes out—assuming it's not delayed, which would make it a rarity among CD Projekt games. It will also be the same number of years between Witcher 3 and 4 as spanned GTA 5 and 6. In the world of technology, 13 years is a long time.

Hell, just the upgrade from the original Witcher 3 to the remastered version that dropped earlier this year is notable:.

At the same time, Nowakowski remarked that while the GTA 6 launch was tremendously successful, CD Projekt Red doesn't intend to merely mimic Rockstar's approach when The Witcher 4 is ready to go: "Our games are different and the require a certain different approach, and we just do certain things differently than they do.".

Keep up to date with the most notable stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

He also said that while the release of GTA 6 has had an impact on Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 sales on consoles, he doesn't expect it to have a "material impact" on the tech giant's Q4 finances for one obvious reason.

"You do have to remember that a lot of our players are also PC-based," Nowakowski said. "GTA has not introduced on PC. We have not seen any impact whatsoever on the PC sales on engagement." And, he added, "on the PS5 and Xbox, it's not like our sales came to zero.".

Nowakowsi also said that GTA 6 hasn't changed CD Projekt's ambitions for The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2: If anything, it's "an inspiration in many ways for our developers." And he's not concerned about its success pushing up development budgets, because CD Projekt's games "are not budget-driven developments.".

In a recent development, "I'm not saying that we don't care about the budgets. We do, and I'm pretty sure [Rockstar] did as well," Nowakowski remarked. "But you cannot make games like that having in mind, 'This is the fixed number of money I want to spend, and that's it. Otherwise, we're gone.'.

"They are ambition-driven developments and money is important. The budgets are not indefinite. That's not what we're saying. But the philosophy is kind of like I said. And honestly, that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6's release. It has just always been like that.".

Nowakowski's positive take on GTA 6 isn't too far off that of Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski, who stated yesterday that he's suffering from "GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression," although he swiftly clarified that CD Projekt is "doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor." (And that he wasn't being serious about cancelling Cyberpunk 2.).

It has been revealed that seriously though i think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor. GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed.

The Witcher 4 is at the moment slated for launch sometime in 2028, while Cyberpunk 2 isn't expected out before 2030.

Sources indicate that since hearing about the upcoming Baywatch reboot, Baena wanted to get in on the action. And while he didn’t get the opportunity to audition until the show had already started and the slow motion-running was already in full swing, he was able to snag an appearance in one of the 12 episodes that will debut in January 2027. While on set to shoot an episode of Celebrity Weakest Link, he told Us Magazine:.

Industry observers note that I’m Livvy Dunne’s boyfriend in the show. And she was amazing — such a great talent and she was such a talented and special gymnast. To see her in Baywatch was great.

Sources indicate that upon joining Baywatch’s cast, model Livvy Dunne put on one of the iconic red swimsuits and got to work alongside the OGs, also making appearances. It sounds like Joseph Baena was quite impressed with the work the cast has put in.

Sources indicate that if the BTS Baywatch content is any indication, the cast of the reboot, who were already physically fit, has been going through rigorous training to not only prepare for their roles, but to maintain that strength and endurance for an entire season. According to recent reports, she killed it. As did the rest of the cast. Thaddeus [LaGrone], Noah Beck and everyone else is doing a phenomenal job. It was amazing to spend time with them on set and work out with them on set. I’m just really excited for the episode to come out of the whole show.

  • The largest hub of all that activity has been the Project Leonida Discord server, which had its own repository and a team of volunteer modders working - with help from Claude AI - to recompile GTA 6's leaked Xbox build to run on PC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A lot has happened in the last 24 hours in the community working to get Grand Theft Auto 6 running on PC. And now, Rockstar has dealt a major blow to their efforts.

Industry observers note that after infamous leaker CyberLeek made good on their promise and released a full Xbox build of GTA 6, the build immediately spread online amongst modders and recompilers. Their goal? Get the game playable on PC as soon as possible.

The largest hub of all that activity has been the Project Leonida Discord server, which had its own repository and a team of volunteer modders working - with help from Claude AI - to recompile GTA 6's leaked Xbox build to run on PC. Rockstar has allegedly taken down the server, causing the project's leaders to dismantle the entire operation.

Project Leonida's lead NotRexed posted on X to announce they're ending development, after fans noticed the Discord server has been removed, as has Project Leonida's GitHub repository.

It has been revealed that "I quit guys. I'm sorry," NotRexed wrote. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can't control so I'm stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.".

The modder, who claims to be a "15 year-old kid", later wrote in a follow-up X post that Rockstar is behind the server's takedown, though that's not the only reason for the project's end.

"Last post from me. I wanna clear things up," they wrote. "Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I've said before, I'm a 15 year-old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.".

Before the Project Leonida server disappeared, footage emerged showing GTA 6 running on PC. The game is able to reach the initial setup screen, but quickly goes into a black screen afterwards. As unimpressive as the result was, it was achieved within hours of the full Xbox build's leak.

It has been revealed that incidentally, while Project Leonida was the biggest and most prominent of the various GTA 6 recompilation projects, the leaking of the full Xbox build has given rise to various other groups. PortWatch VI is a website dedicated to tracking their progress, and though the data is almost entirely self-reported, a few other teams appear to have made notable progress themselves, so this may not be the end of the story.

According to recent reports, rockstar has yet to comment publicly on the Xbox build's leak, and the company has not revealed GTA 6 for PC. However, a report suggested GTA 6 arrives on PC in the first quarter of 2027, earlier than everyone expected.

If you're among the millions already playing the game on consoles, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough contains a wealth of information covering all major mechanics, main missions, secrets, cheats and more besides.
